In summary, our research is concerned with
a top-down methodology for designing high-speed monolithic optical receivers based on thin-film SOICMOS.
the design of high-speed, high-sensitivity, low-cost and low-power monolithic integrated optical receivers.
the design of multi Gb/s monolithically integrated optical front-ends in thin-film SOICMOS technology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our design methodology allows one to predict and optimize the architecture and performances (gain, sensitivity, power, noise, area) of monolithically integrated optical front-ends for 1 to10Gb/s short distance communication and Blue DVD applications.
the proposed methodology is very general and can be applied to any type of TIA, single stage or multi stage.

the proposed top-down design methodology allows to predict and design, in a simultaneous way, the photodiode and the transistors of the receiver in order to optimize its performance and to meet the specifications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose here a design procedure for the design of transimpedance and photodiode based on a gm-id approach which is based on a top-down design procedure.
we have developed a top-down design strategy of high speed monolithic integrated receivers for 1-10 Gb/s optical communication or Blue DVD.
we have shown that thin-film SOICMOS technology is a very good candidate to implement high-speed monolithic integrated photoreceiv-ers for short distance applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a careful design of the TIA is mandatory to reach high sensitivity and low noise.
the use of SOI technology and the design of the transimpedancers with the proposed methodologies allow one to achieve high-speed receivers with low power consumption.
, in order to optimize the receiver performances, the design of the photodiode and of the transimpedence amplifier should be done in a simultaneous way.
